primary_antecedent.title: Boundary Problems for Wave Equations With Grazing and Gliding Rays
locators: Section 6.3, equation 6.3.28 and its adjacent decaying-kernel decomposition
primary_antecedent.receiving_contribution: Independent ordinary homogeneous FIO proof of the sharp variable-coefficient decaying Airy collar estimate, positive normal symbol, reverse estimate and sharpness.

source_correspondence: The receiving operator is the actual unnormalized variable-phase Ai kernel with classical matrix coefficients, compact base/conic support, both covector axes excluded and the exact boundary phase.

The controlled half-line extension preserves every amplitude symbol seminorm and the phase degrees on a signed collar. It is used for restriction-norm estimates; no equation on the negative side is asserted.

The homogeneous auxiliary change retains its Jacobian and the minus sign in g-hs. Differentiated noncompact auxiliary tails have integrable polynomial bounds and arbitrary inverse frequency powers, giving a complete smooth residual.

At the caustic, the output projection differential is injective without division by the fold variable. The input block Jacobian is invertible, giving one-dimensional fibers on a fixed neighborhood. Both covector axes remain excluded.

The base dimension is 2d+1 and the phase dimension d+1, so kernel order is -5/12. The adjoint composition is clean with excess one. Compact amplitude support, not compactness of the full open geometric fiber, is explicitly justified through the existing complete local composition proof.

The full all-real Sobolev argument uses exact supported elliptic weights and smoothing parametrices, with an order-zero normal operator. It retains all smooth errors and identifies the bounded completion with the distributional kernel.

A fixed interior branch has a quantitatively invertible mixed phase matrix, a nonzero stationary constant and an invertible matrix amplitude. Its normal symbol is the actual positive graph-fiber Gram integral with determinant and output Sobolev weight.

A supported matrix parametrix gives the reverse estimate with a coarse remainder and proves regularity on the original distributional domain. Fixed localized oscillatory packets prove sharpness for every real target order.

Three complete solutions give the full affine relation and inverse projection, exact leading L2 and energy powers with a remainder, and a variable-base half-density example. Twenty-nine exact finite algebraic checks verify signs, ranks, orders and covector identities; they do not replace the analytic proof.

The complete general Airy energy representation, growing-mode coefficient domain, general-manifold scalar observation assembly and all remaining HIII21/23/24 and HIV25/26 obligations remain active. Required human foundation proofs remain external.
